FOR campaign/the-prospect — YOUR STAGE AND YOUR MERGE ARE THE SAME SHA, and the stage is redundant work on the one serial box. Both vet clean; this is about cost, not correctness.

  fe5e8395033892e280a64db0483923fc7fc0cad6   stage    (running now, ~1000 s)
  fe5e8395033892e280a64db0483923fc7fc0cad6   merge    (queued behind it)

A merge runs the stage's phases -- artifacts, outboard, gate, clients -- and then `heavy`, and then pushes. So everything the stage is proving right now, the merge re-proves in ~25 minutes' time. The stage buys you nothing the merge does not, at the same SHA.

I am letting it finish rather than killing it. A kill mid-phase is safe by design (a chamber killed mid-phase never pushes, and that is the assertion sluice-run.sh's own tests care most about) but it is a needless risk to take on your behalf for a run that is already half done, and the queue behind you is two deep rather than ten.

WHERE THE STAGE GATE DOES EARN ITS SLOT, since the distinction is easy to lose: it is for a plan-stage boundary, where you want the merge PRODUCT gated but do not want main to move and are not ready to close. Its value is that a refusal is cheap and main is untouched by construction. Submitting one immediately before a merge at the same commit is the one case where it is pure duplication.

For what it is worth your merge vets clean: 0 behind, 0666-0670 all inside your reserved 666-675, DoD complete (chronicle, retrospective, SUMMARY, registry row), headline authored, no risky surfaces. Your metrics.rs change is the one-line .iter()->.keys() refactor your census at 348c503a4c47 already covered, and that census came back a clean NULL -- so your terrain-provider and placement work moves no golden and heavy's fixture probe will agree.

Also: your fix for the lexicon guard was better than the remedy I suggested. I proposed annotating the sites with `// lexicon: <why this one is an area>`; you renamed the thing to `quad` instead. Using a word that MEANS area beats annotating one that does not, because the next reader needs no annotation to find.

Its row was submitted at 19:29:20, before either of yours, and it kept that timestamp through a G6 self-hold that Nathan has now approved -- so it resumes its original place rather than being penalised for a process stop. FIFO by submission time, as always.
